# p10k-rs v0.1.7 — DRAFT

> Status: **draft** — pending Sean's review. Replace this banner
> and tag when ready. The release workflow fires on
> `git push origin v0.1.7`.

**The "close out slice 60" release.** GixBackend reaches full
feature parity with what the gitstatusd backend ships in MVP:
per-category status counts, ahead/behind tracking, and a
cross-checked + benchmarked equivalence with the ShellOut tier.
Plus a convenience slice — `install.sh` now downloads the
MesloLGS NF fonts (default-on, sha256-pinned, WSL-aware).

**Test count:** 559 passing, 3 ignored (544 at v0.1.6).
**Slice count:** 5 code commits + 2 docs commits since v0.1.6.
**Theme:** "GixBackend at full parity + ergonomic installer."

## What you'll notice (visible changes)

### Fonts install by default

A fresh `./install.sh` run now downloads the four MesloLGS NF
variants (Regular / Bold / Italic / Bold Italic) into the right
OS-specific font directory, pinned to a specific commit of
`romkatv/powerlevel10k-media` with per-file sha256 verification:

- **Linux** → `~/.local/share/fonts/p10k-rs/` + `fc-cache -f`.
- **macOS** → `~/Library/Fonts/` (ATS auto-registers; no
  `fc-cache` needed).
- **WSL** → **skipped** with explicit Windows-side install
  instructions. The Linux-side font dir is invisible to the
  Windows terminal that actually renders your prompt, so
  shipping fonts to it would silently do the wrong thing for
  most WSL users. The installer detects WSL via
  `/proc/sys/kernel/osrelease` and tells you to install the
  fonts via Windows instead.

Existing installs are respected — if `fc-list` already shows
MesloLGS NF (e.g. you installed via package manager, oh-my-posh,
or a previous P10K wizard), the download is skipped. Opt out
entirely with `./install.sh --no-fonts`. Network failures and
sha256 mismatches degrade to "warn and continue" — fonts never
break the installer.

THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md documents the Apache-2.0 (Meslo LG) /
MIT (Nerd Fonts patches) license split and the fetch-don't-bundle
redistribution stance (we never ship the font files inside the
repo or release tarballs; the installer fetches them at user-
initiated install time, matching how upstream P10K's wizard
handles the same files on iTerm2 and Termux).

### VCS prompt now shows full state in stripped containers

v0.1.6 landed branch / dirty / action on the GixBackend tier so
the prompt didn't lose its VCS indicator on hosts without `git`.
v0.1.7 extends that to the richer state every modern prompt
reader expects:

```
~/work/repo on main ✗ ↑2 *3 +1 ?5   # GixBackend: ahead 2, unstaged 3, staged 1, untracked 5
```

| Field | gitstatusd | ShellOut | GixBackend (v0.1.6) | GixBackend (v0.1.7) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `branch` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| `dirty` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| `action` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| `staged` / `unstaged` / `untracked` / `conflicts` | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | **✓** |
| `ahead` / `behind` | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | **✓** |

The fallback chain (`gitstatusd → ShellOut → GixBackend`) is
unchanged. Hosts with `git` on `$PATH` never reach the gix tier,
so there's no perf hit for the common case.

### Theme catalogue + `p10k-rs theme {list, show, install}`

Ten bundled themes ship inside the binary (lean / classic /
rainbow / pure / catppuccin-mocha / tokyo-night / gruvbox-dark /
nord / solarized-dark / dracula). New subcommand:

```bash
p10k-rs theme list                       # catalogue
p10k-rs theme show dracula               # dump TOML to stdout
p10k-rs theme install catppuccin-mocha   # write to ~/.config/p10k-rs/config.toml
```

`install` backs up your existing config to `<path>.bak` unless
`--force` is given. 5 new unit tests including
`every_bundled_theme_parses` — a regression marker for the
schema-enum-casing inconsistencies (see
`feedback_schema_enum_naming` in maintainer memory).

## What you won't notice (but matters)

### Bench: GixBackend is ~12× faster than ShellOut

The slice 60 phase 6 criterion bench measures per-call
`.status(workspace_root)` latency on the workspace itself:

```
git_backend/gix_workspace        ~2.1 ms / iter
git_backend/shellout_workspace  ~26.7 ms / iter
```

Most of the gap is the per-prompt `fork`/`execve` overhead
ShellOut pays to spawn `git`; the gix path stays in-process.
This validates ADR-0001's premise (daemon > shell-out) and
confirms the pure-Rust tier is fast enough to be a genuine
fallback, not just a "correctness when git is absent" lifeline.

Run it yourself:

```bash
cargo bench -p p10k-rs-git --bench git_backend
```

Outputs land in `target/criterion/`, with an HTML report at
`target/criterion/git_backend/report/index.html`.

### Cross-check tests guard parity going forward

`crates/p10k-rs-git/tests/cross_check.rs` asserts that for the
same on-disk repo state, ShellOut and GixBackend agree on the
fields ShellOut populates (`branch` + `dirty`). Six fixtures
cover clean / untracked / modified / staged / ahead-of-upstream /
detached-HEAD repos.

The detached-HEAD case is the **documented known divergence**:
ShellOut returns the literal string `"HEAD"` (it parses
`## HEAD (no branch)` from `git status --porcelain=v1`); gix
returns the 7-char short OID (which is what gitstatusd and
upstream P10K render). The test explicitly asserts the
divergence shape so a future ShellOut rewrite that lifts to
short-OID rendering will FAIL the test and prompt a deliberate
cleanup, rather than silently agreeing.

Per-category counts and ahead/behind aren't in the cross-check
because ShellOut leaves them at zero today (it only fills
`branch` + `dirty` from porcelain v1). Lifting ShellOut to fill
those is a candidate v0.1.8 slice.

### Render-path sanitisation chokepoint (unchanged)

Every byte the gix backend produces still flows through
`SafeText`. The new per-category counts and ahead/behind are
`u32`s so they bypass the string sanitiser by construction;
the existing branch + detached-OID sanitisation paths are
unchanged.

### No new gix features required

Phase 4 (ahead/behind) used `Repository::rev_walk(tips)
.with_hidden(others)` — the gix-traverse equivalent of
`git rev-list A ^B`. The higher-level `merge_base` APIs are
gated behind the `revision` feature; we didn't need that, so
the gix feature set stays at `["sha1", "status"]` and the
transitive package count doesn't grow.

## How to verify (unchanged from v0.1.5)

Same recipe — every tarball ships with a sigstore keyless
signature plus SLSA build-provenance attestation. After install,
`p10k-rs verify` re-hashes gitstatusd against the committed pin.

```bash
cosign verify-blob \
  --bundle p10k-rs-v0.1.7-<triple>.tar.gz.cosign.bundle \
  --certificate-identity-regexp \
    'https://github.com/scurran1986/powerlevel10k-rs/\.github/workflows/release\.ya?ml@refs/tags/v0\.1\.7' \
  --certificate-oidc-issuer 'https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com' \
  p10k-rs-v0.1.7-<triple>.tar.gz

gh attestation verify p10k-rs-v0.1.7-<triple>.tar.gz \
  --owner scurran1986

p10k-rs verify
```

All must succeed. See [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).

## Migration

No breaking changes. New `install.sh` font flow is default-on
and idempotent; users who don't want it pass `--no-fonts`.
Existing MesloLGS NF installations from any other source are
detected and respected.

The vcs segment now displays per-category counters and
ahead/behind on GixBackend-served hosts where it previously
displayed only branch + dirty. Users who relied on the absence
of those decorations as an implicit signal can suppress them
via the existing per-segment config (`[segment.vcs].show_counts`,
etc.).

## Deferred to v0.1.8

- **Per-host statusline contracts** — `cursor`, `aider`, `goose`
  currently fall through to `""` in `render_statusline`. Pattern
  is `claude-code-statusline-contract.md` in planning research;
  each host gets its own contract note + implementation.
- **T1.8 follow-up** — real `UniqueDir` history semantics
  (currently aliased to `SameDir`). Needs cross-prompt cwd
  history machinery in `init.zsh`.
- **Slice 64** — daemon-respawn / health-check cache (ADR-0001
  § Follow-ups). Still design-doc-only.
- **ShellOut per-category counts** — would tighten the cross-check
  tests; not currently implemented (porcelain v1 parser only
  fills `dirty: bool`).
